summary: LunarPulse is an interactive tool to help identify promising landing sites on the Moon. It pulls together NASA's data on one map, factors in moonquake likelihood temperature sunlight and water ice in the vicinity and, for the landing site, ranks them for comparison. It also adds the NASA and JPL lunar ephemeris to show where the Sun and Earth will be for the next 30 days. Perform P- and S-wave simulations and verify that the Sun and Earth are both visible. The goal: Making Artemis site selection a little less like an Easter egg hunt, and putting all of NASA's lunar data in one handy, interactive package.
details:
LunarPulse – Interactive Lunar Landing Site Analysis Platform

1. Problem Explanation and Project Purpose

As humanity moves closer to returning to the Moon through NASAs Artemis program choosing the right landing site becomes a critical step. The Moons surface is not easy to work on. It has challenges that can make missions harder or even unsafe.

Landing sites must be carefully checked. They need to be safe for landers and rovers. They must support long-term operations. Some of the concerns include moonquakes, extreme cold and heat how much sunlight a site gets and how close it is to water ice.

Moonquakes can shake the ground and damage structures. The Moon has no atmosphere so temperatures swing wildly between day and night. Equipment can fail if it does not get sunlight for power. Water ice if found nearby could be used for drinking water, oxygen or fuel. So finding a site with water ice is very helpful.

LunarPulse was created to help solve this problem. It is a web-based platform that brings together different kinds of data about the Moon into one place. The goal is to make it easier to evaluate landing locations. The platform uses data from NASA’s CLPS program to help users explore and analyze spots on the Moon.


2. Technical Implementation and Main Features

LunarPulse combines scientific data with 3D interactive tools to give users a full picture of lunar landing conditions. One of its tools is a simulation of the Sun and Earth over a 30-day period. This uses ephemeris algorithms and data from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL).

The simulation shows where the Sun and Earth appear in the sky from any point on the Moon. It helps users see how long a site gets sunlight and how often Earth is visible. This is important because solar power depends on sunlight and communication with Earth depends on visibility.

Another feature lets users pick any location on the Moon by entering coordinates. The platform then gives a suitability score for that area. The score is based on factors like temperature, sunlight, seismic activity and water ice availability. This helps compare sites quickly.

LunarPulse also shows how seismic waves move through the Moon’s surface. It simulates P-waves and S-waves which're the two main types of moonquake waves. Users can see how these waves spread out from a source area. This helps them understand the risk of ground shaking at a landing site.

The platform also includes tools for solar illumination and Earth visibility. These help users see what the environment is like at times. By combining all these tools into one 3D lunar environment LunarPulse makes it easier to explore and understand information.

3. Project Objectives and Expected Impact

The main goal of LunarPulse is to make lunar landing site evaluation simpler, clearer and faster. Of looking at seismic data, temperature data and solar data in separate reports users can view them all together in one place.

This integrated approach supports mission planning, risk assessment and the search for locations for long-term operations. For example scientists and engineers can use the platform to compare two sites and decide which one is safer and more practical.

LunarPulse is meant to be both a tool and a planning tool. It shows how real scientific datasets, astronomical calculations and 3D technology can work together to solve problems in space exploration.

4. Overall Conclusion

LunarPulse offers a way to understand the challenges of landing on the Moon. It brings together data on activity, temperature, sunlight and resources into a single interactive system. This helps make mission planning more efficient and reduces risks.

By turning data into a clear, visual and easy-to-use platform LunarPulse supports the development of safer more sustainable missions. It is a step, in how we prepare for future exploration of the Moon.
